=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Position Review (Buyer Perspective)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package shifts almost all known risk to Wattlebridge. It caps general recovery at AUD 4.8m (20%), subjects title and tax to the same limits, and excludes claims on anything in the data room or public records. Since the Seller has also disclosed the known problems, Wattlebridge would have little recourse for them unless they are dealt with through specific indemnities, price adjustments, or conditions. Those protections need to be in the mark-up.

**Caveats:** I have reviewed the Seller's cover summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA text. Clause references need checking against the actual draft. The disclosure is stated as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026, so the position may have moved. Have NSW counsel confirm the legal points flagged below, especially limitation periods, sandbagging, and privacy obligations.

---

## 1. Warranty protection and limits

| Seller position | Why it's adverse | Pushback |
|---|---|---|
| **General cap: 20% (AUD 4.8m)** (cl 12.1) | Low for a AUD 24m deal. The cap is about equal to the quantified known exposures (see section 4), so little would remain for unknown risks. | Cap at 100% of price for general warranties, or at least 50%. |
| **De minimis AUD 25k per claim; basket AUD 250k, recovery only of the excess** (cl 12.2) | An excess-only basket means Wattlebridge absorbs the first AUD 250k of every claim. Combined with the de minimis, many small but related claims go unrecovered. | Lower de minimis (e.g. AUD 10k) with aggregation of related claims. Tipping basket: once exceeded, recovery is from the first dollar. Basket of about 0.5–1% of price. |
| **18-month general claim period** (cl 12.3/13) | Too short for a business with an audit cycle, tax assessments, and IP ownership questions that may only surface later. | 36 months for general warranties. Tax, title, and fundamental warranties on longer periods (see below). |
| **Any limitation applies to all claims** (cl 12.3/13) | Would pull fundamental, tax, and fraud claims into the 18-month window and general cap. | Reject. Fundamental, tax, and fraud claims should sit outside general limits. |
| **Capacity and title subject to the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity"** | Title is the core asset. If the Seller cannot deliver clean title, the buyer has bought nothing. | Reject. Title and capacity capped at 100% of price, with a limitation period of at least six years (confirm under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW), which should be checked against whether the SPA is executed as a deed). |
| **Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime"** | Tax assessments can run for four years or more, and IP ownership issues can surface after the general period has expired. | Specific pre-Completion tax indemnity, with a claim period of the ATO amendment period plus 60 days. Separate IP warranties on a longer period, outside the general cap. |

---

## 2. Exclusions that defeat recovery

- **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims** (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). This would catch fraud and fundamental claims. Carve out fraud (which non-reliance clauses generally cannot exclude in any case), title, capacity, tax, and specific indemnities.
- **Buyer knowledge bar** (cl 8.3). The Seller would bar any claim where Wattlebridge or its advisers "had knowledge", including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records". This is a strong anti-sandbagging position. Combined with the disclosures, it would bar recovery for nearly every identified issue. Reject. Insert a pro-sandbagging clause, or at minimum make the specific indemnities expressly apply notwithstanding Wattlebridge's knowledge.
- **General disclosure of the data room and public registers** (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2). Disclosing the entire data room, the accounts, and public registers would qualify every warranty against everything in those documents. Warranties should be qualified only by specific, fair disclosure, with reasonable particularity, against a specified warranty. Reject the general disclosure.

---

## 3. Specific matters

**Bluefen (about 30% of FY26 revenue, AUD 3.6m).** The Seller proposes to "use reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent exists and the cl 11.3 conditions are unsatisfied.
- Written, unconditional Bluefen consent, with the cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, should be a condition precedent to Completion, not a matter for endeavours.
- If Bluefen terminates or imposes adverse conditions, Wattlebridge should have a walk right or a price adjustment, and a specific indemnity for any loss.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m outstanding, change control 8.1, discharge 9.2).** The Seller plans to provide a release after Completion. Under a debt-free/cash-free deal, the seller should repay the facility from the price at Completion.
- Payoff letter and discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations) delivered at Completion.
- Funds flow to show the payoff, and confirm whether Riverlark's change-control consent is needed.

**Ironquay IP (SOW 3, AUD 180k open).** The Seller's indemnity is limited to the SOW 3 payment and called "adequate". Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW 3 Project Materials transfers only once every SOW 3 fee is cleared, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- Seller to pay the AUD 180k (or the amount is deducted as a debt-like item) before Completion, and to deliver a confirmatory assignment of the Project Materials as a CP.
- A specific IP indemnity covering ownership and third-party claims, outside the cap and basket, with a retention or escrow until the assignment is registered or confirmed.

**Employee bonuses (AUD 420k, DD-005).** The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but they are not in the funds flow. These are debt-like items in substance.
- Treat as a Seller cost deducted from price, including any employer on-costs. Indicatively, super at 12% and NSW payroll tax at about 5.45% would add roughly AUD 70k, bringing the total closer to AUD 490k, subject to confirming whether each applies.
- Confirm whether the bonuses are triggered by the change of control and whether they are conditional on continued employment after Completion.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006, about 1,240 records).** The Seller calls this a "preliminary operational matter" that is "not expected to be material". This characterisation sits uneasily with the disclosure, which records names, business emails, roles, and timestamps being sent to an unintended external address, with no conclusion on whether anyone accessed it.
- Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) (Part IIIC), an eligible data breach may require notification to the OAIC and affected individuals. The assessment must generally be done within 30 days of suspicion. Given the 22 September date and today's date, this timing needs urgent review.
- Require: a forensic investigation report, a documented Privacy Act assessment, a specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity for notification costs, regulatory action, and third-party claims, and a warranty on data handling. Consider an escrow until the investigation closes.

**Office lease (DD-007).** Confirm whether landlord consent is required for the share sale. If it is, obtain consent or a waiver as a CP. If only a notice obligation, obtain evidence of notice and no default.

**Supplier renewals (AUD 330k aggregate, DD-008 and DD-011).** The Seller calls these ordinary course, but three renewals of AUD 110k each, read together, look like a single commitment split into parts.
- Confirm whether any are new commitments entered after the signing date (which an interim covenant should prohibit without consent), and whether they are terminable.
- Treat any non-ordinary-course amounts as debt-like or a Seller cost.

**Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller does not say whether consent is needed because of the share sale. Obtain written confirmation from Mossvale, or a legal opinion, that no consent is required, or make consent a CP.

**Title (DD-012).** The share register showing Harbourglass as holder of 100% is a starting point, not verification. Wattlebridge should run its own ASIC company search, check the register and minute books, confirm there are no options or rights over shares, check PPSR for encumbrances over shares and assets, and inspect original share certificates. Title should be a fundamental warranty on the terms above.

---

## 4. Exposure snapshot

| Item | Indicative AUD | Current Seller treatment | Recommended treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | 3,200,000 | Released after Completion | Repaid from price at Completion |
| Employee bonuses (plus on-costs) | 420,000 (about 490,000 with on-costs) | Excluded from funds flow | Seller cost, deducted from price |
| Ironquay SOW 3 | 180,000 | Indemnity limited to that payment | Paid pre-Completion or deducted; IP indemnity |
| Supplier renewals | 330,000 | "Ordinary course" | Interim covenant; treat non-ordinary items as debt-like |
| Privacy incident | Unknown | "Not material" | Specific indemnity, escrow |
| Bluefen revenue at risk | About 3,600,000 revenue | Endeavours; deemed satisfied | CP; walk right or price adjustment |

The quantified debt-like and specific items total roughly AUD 4.1m before the privacy exposure is quantified, which is close to the AUD 4.8m general cap. Under the Seller's draft, most of this would be unrecoverable.

---

## 5. Recommendations (prioritised)

1. **Move the known issues out of the warranty regime.** Use price deductions, Completion deliverables, and specific indemnities outside the cap, basket, and disclosure. This is the most important point.
2. **Reject the general disclosure and the buyer-knowledge bar.** Insert a pro-sandbagging clause.
3. **Make the Bluefen consent and Riverlark discharge conditions precedent**, with walk rights if not met.
4. **Fix the funds flow**: repay Riverlark at Completion, and deduct the bonuses (with on-costs) and the Ironquay amount.
5. **Escalate the privacy incident** to forensic investigation and Privacy Act assessment now, with a specific indemnity and escrow.
6. **Restructure the limits:** general cap to 100% (or at least 50%) of price, tipping basket of about 0.5–1%, 36-month general period, fundamental and title warranties capped at price with a six-year period, separate tax indemnity to the ATO amendment period plus 60 days.
7. **Reject the title/tax/IP "simplicity" positions** and the exclusive-remedy extension to fraud and fundamental claims.
8. **Confirm third-party consents**: lease (landlord), Mossvale, and the Bluefen change-control conditions.
9. **Consider a W&I policy** to supplement negotiated protections, though known matters are typically excluded from cover and so will still need specific indemnities.
10. **Request an updated Disclosure Letter** as at the current date, and an updated data room index, since the Seller's position is six weeks old.

**Priority information requests:** the full SPA mark-up; the Bluefen change-control correspondence and cl 11.3 conditions; a Riverlark payoff statement; a DD-006 incident report with timeline; a Company PPSR and ASIC search; the SOW 3 contract and payment history; the bonus plan documents; the Mossvale and landlord consent provisions.
